metaDescription: Enable subscription products in Squarespace: create the product, set the billing frequency and discount, and get recurring revenue flowing.
intro: Recurring revenue changes the math on a small store — instead of chasing one-off sales, you get predictable income from customers who've already committed. Squarespace builds subscriptions directly into its commerce tools, so a membership box, a recurring digital drop, or a subscribe-and-save version of a physical product doesn't need a third-party app. The setup lives inside the product editor rather than a separate "subscriptions" menu, which is the part that trips people up first. This guide walks through where that setting actually is, how the frequency and discount options work, and what to check before you turn subscriptions on for real customers.

steps.heading: Open your Squarespace dashboard
steps.body: Log in and land on the Dashboard tab, which lists every site tied to your account with its domain and trial or plan status. Pick the site you want to sell subscriptions on and open it — subscriptions are configured per site, inside that site's own commerce settings, not from this top-level account screen. If you manage more than one site, double-check you're editing the right one before you start building a product, since it's easy to open the wrong project from a list like this.

image.caption: The Squarespace account dashboard, listing each site with its domain and trial status. Subscriptions get configured inside a specific site, not from here.

steps.heading: Create or open the product you want to sell as a subscription
steps.body: Subscriptions in Squarespace aren't a separate product category — they're a purchase option you add to a regular product. Open an existing product or start a new one, and you'll land on the standard product editor: an Images panel for photos, and an Inventory section with Price, an On Sale toggle, and stock settings. Fill in the basics the same way you would for a one-time item, since the subscription behavior gets layered on top of this same product rather than replacing it.

image.caption: The standard product editor — images, price, and stock. Subscription options are added on top of this same product, not created separately.

steps.heading: Choose between one-time and subscription purchasing
steps.body: Below the basic product details, Squarespace gives you a purchase-type choice: let customers pick between a one-time purchase or a recurring one, or restrict the product to "Subscription only" so it can only be bought as a recurring order. Which one you pick depends on the product — subscription-only makes sense for a membership or a box that only exists as a recurring offer, while the choice option suits a physical product you also sell individually, like coffee or skincare that some customers want once and others want on repeat.

steps.heading: Set the billing frequency and cycle
steps.body: Once subscriptions are enabled, a Frequency section appears where you set how often the order repeats — a number paired with a unit like Week or Month — and a Billing Cycle dropdown that controls how long the subscription runs, including a "Never Expires" option for an ongoing plan. Pick intervals that match how the product actually gets used: weekly for something consumable, monthly for a membership or digital drop. Getting this wrong is one of the most common subscription complaints, so match the cadence to how fast a customer would realistically want a refill or renewal.

image.caption: The Frequency settings for a subscription product — how often it repeats, the billing cycle, and an optional discount for subscribers.

steps.heading: Add a subscriber discount
steps.body: The same panel includes a Discount field, entered as a percentage, that Squarespace applies automatically to every recurring order on that plan. This is the standard lever for making a subscription worth committing to — a modest discount, even five or ten percent, is often enough to convert a one-time buyer into a subscriber, since it rewards the commitment without eating your margin on every single unit. Add it here rather than through a separate promotion, since a subscription-specific discount applies consistently to every renewal without needing to be reissued.

steps.heading: Confirm checkout and payment settings
steps.body: Recurring orders only work if your store can actually charge a saved payment method automatically, so before launching, verify your payment processor is fully connected and that recurring billing is enabled at the account level, not just on the individual product. Walk through a test purchase if you can, so you see exactly what a customer experiences when they choose the subscription option at checkout versus a one-time buy.

steps.heading: Manage subscribers and renewals going forward
steps.body: Once real subscribers start signing up, Squarespace's order and customer tools let you see who's on an active subscription, when their next renewal is due, and handle cancellations or payment failures as they come in. Check this regularly, especially in the first few weeks after launch, since failed renewal payments are the main reason subscription revenue quietly leaks — catching a declined card early is much easier than trying to win back a lapsed subscriber later.

faq.question: Where do I turn on subscriptions in Squarespace — is there a dedicated menu?
faq.answer: No separate subscriptions menu exists. You enable it inside the product editor for a specific product, choosing between a one-time purchase, a customer's choice of one-time or recurring, or subscription-only.

faq.question: Can I offer both one-time and subscription purchases for the same product?
faq.answer: Yes. Instead of Subscription only, choose the option that lets customers pick between a one-time purchase or a recurring one at checkout, and both prices and frequencies apply to the same product listing.

faq.question: How does the subscriber discount work?
faq.answer: You set a percentage discount in the Frequency section that Squarespace applies automatically to every recurring order on that plan, without needing a separate promo code.

faq.question: What billing frequencies can I offer?
faq.answer: You set a repeat number paired with a unit such as Week or Month, plus a billing cycle that controls how long the plan runs — including an option that never expires for an ongoing subscription.

faq.question: What should I check before launching a subscription product?
faq.answer: Confirm your payment processor supports recurring charges and that automatic billing is active at the account level, then run a test purchase so you can see the subscription checkout flow exactly as a customer would.
